old: Its ancestor word literally meant 'a little head' in Latin — a small top piece standing in for a whole section.
It once named both a book division and a formal council of officials in Medieval Latin.
It's a linguistic cousin of 'capital' and 'capitulum,' both rooted in the Latin word for head.
clues: This noun for a division of a larger whole traces back to a Latin word meaning 'little head.'
It is one of the main numbered divisions of a book, bigger than a paragraph and often given its own title. In Medieval Latin, the word also named a church council.
Starting a new one means beginning a fresh phase of life, a club's local branch is called one, and citing something precisely is giving '___ and verse.'
